taxonomy: Lookup function · Excel and Google Sheets
summary: Finds a value in the first column of a table and hands back something from the same row.

figure.caption: Each argument is washed in the color of the part of the table it controls; the hatched column is never read.

field_marks.label: Lookup value
field_marks.detail: What you're searching for. Here, the item name sitting in A2.

field_marks.label: Table range
field_marks.detail: Where to search. Its first column must hold the values you're matching against.

field_marks.label: Column index
field_marks.detail: Which column to bring back, counted from the left edge of the range, starting at 1.

field_marks.label: Match mode
field_marks.detail: FALSE means exact match. Leave it out and VLOOKUP quietly settles for a near miss.

habitat: Price lists, rosters, inventories: any sheet that pulls details from a reference table
Older workbooks; it predates XLOOKUP by decades
Wherever one sheet looks up a code that lives in another
behavior: Reads the lookup value from A2
Scans the first column of Prices!A:C from the top
Stops at the first exact match
Counts across to column 3 and returns that cell

similar.name: XLOOKUP
similar.tell_apart: Can look left as well as right, and defaults to exact match. Prefer it in Excel 365.

similar.name: HLOOKUP
similar.tell_apart: The same idea turned on its side: it searches the first row.
similar.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 160 90"><rect x="8" y="6" width="144" height="54" class="p1s"/><rect x="8" y="6" width="144" height="18" class="p3s"/><path d="M8 24 H152 M8 42 H152 M56 6 V60 M104 6 V60" class="leader"/><rect x="8" y="6" width="144" height="54" class="outline"/><path d="M14 15 H146" class="flow"/><text x="80" y="82" text-anchor="middle" class="label-2">searches the top row</text></svg>

field_note: Your cell D4 runs =VLOOKUP(A2, Prices!A:C, 3, FALSE), so it fills in Pear's price, $1.20. Insert a column in Prices and that 3 will quietly point at the wrong one.
